notes:
Zero turn starts. The whole fragment sits inside one continuous speech: the annual message of the President of the Nation to the Legislative Assembly. The full sitting file shows the last label before this fragment is "Sr. PRESIDENTE DE LA NACIÓN.-", and the speech runs on past the closing words ("Muchas cosas pasaron y nos pasaron en estos diez años..."), so nothing starts here. Not one bold run appears in the fragment. Markup differs from the Senate sittings: paragraphs are lowercase "

", never closed, and there is no FONT wrapper. The nine events are all applause notes and all parenthesised rather than dash-opened. They come in three different markups, which a parser keyed on the italic run alone will read differently: one fully inside the italic including the parentheses ("(Pónense de pie los legisladores. ...)"), five with the parentheses outside and the full stop outside too ("(Aplausos.)"), and three with the full stop inside ("(Aplausos.)"). All eight short ones print identically as "(Aplausos.)", which is how I recorded them; the order in the list is the order on the page. Flagging one judgement: I treated all nine as events rather than as part of the president's speech, including the five where only the word Aplausos is italicised and the punctuation sits in the surrounding roman run. Nobody utters them, and the mixed markup is typist inconsistency, not a distinction in kind. No headings, no furniture, no inserted document. CORRECTED — EVENTS NOW EMPTY: under the corpus convention (TODO.md Phase 2) an event is a note printed as its OWN paragraph, and an italic fragment sitting inside a speaker's paragraph is merged back into that speech instead of splitting the turn (the PDF side calls this block type inline_italic). I checked all nine against the markup and every one of them is inline: each closes one of the president's own paragraphs and the next "

" opens his next one. That includes the long opening note, which I checked rather than assumed — "(Pónense de pie los legisladores. Aplausos prolongados y manifestaciones en las bancas y en las galerías.)" ends the paragraph that finishes "¡Viva la Argentina! ¡Viva Chile!", so it does not stand alone either. Not one italic run in this fragment occupies a paragraph of its own. They are therefore reclassified as inline fragments of the president's speech, NOT judged unreal: the applause happened and the stenographer set it down, it simply belongs to his turn rather than interrupting it. The three-markup observation above stands and is the reason the reclassification is worth recording. Consequence for scoring: this fragment now expects zero turn starts AND zero events, so anything a parser emits here is a false positive.
